The American College of Lifestyle Medicine (ACLM) is the medical professional association for physicians

and other professionals dedicated to clinical and worksite practice of lifestyle medicine as the foundation of

a transformed and sustainable healthcare system. ACLM is a galvanizing force for change. ACLM addresses

the need for quality, evidence-based education and certification as well as advocates for its members in their
individual practices and in their collective mission to nationally and globally promote lifestyle medicine as the first
and optimal treatment option. ACLM members are united in their desire to eradicate the root causes of chronic
disease. Rather than disease management, lifestyle medicine clinicians specialize in health restoration.

AUTHORS

JENI SHULL CLAYTON,
MD, MPH, DipABLM,
FACLM

Jeni Shull Clayton is a
family, preventive, and
lifestyle medicine physician.
She is a certified medical
review officer, DOT/CDL medical examiner, and
professional supervisor for audiometric monitoring
programs. Dr. Clayton has led teams in making
lifestyle medicine the foundation of practice at
employer wellness and occupational medicine
Clinics and a traditional family medicine clinic.

Dr. Clayton graduated from Indiana University School
of Medicine. She attended Loma Linda University’s
Family and Preventive Medicine residency, where
she served as chief resident and completed her
Master's in Population Health. She was awarded
Resident Teacher of the Year and the Will Alexander
Whole Person Care Award. Under Dr. John Kelly,
founder of ACLM, she became the first Lifestyle
Medicine Fellow at the Black Hills Health and
Education Center. She has served as co-author of
the Foundations of Lifestyle Medicine Board Review
Manual and Course since its inception in 2017.

Dr. Clayton also serves as co-chair of the ACLM
Education Committee. She lives in Indiana with her
husband and daughter and enjoys gardening, hiking,
and cooking healthy meals with family and friends.

JONATHAN BONNET,
MD, MPH, DipABOM,
DipABLM, FAAFP, FACLM

Jonathan Bonnet is a
board-certified family,
sports, obesity, and lifestyle
medicine physician. He
works at the Palo Alto VA hospital in their weight
management center. Dr. Bonnet has a background
in exercise physiology and is a certified personal
trainer. He completed his undergraduate and
medical school degrees at Ohio State University
before finishing his family medicine residency at
Duke University and his sports medicine fellowship
at the University of Florida. He also holds a Master's
in Public Health from Harvard.

Dr. Bonnet served on the board of ACLM from 2014-
2016 and currently serves as faculty advisor for the
Emory University Lifestyle Medicine Interest Group.
He has co-authored two editions of the Lifestyle
Medicine Handbook and the first edition of the
Medical Fitness Bible. He has published research
in sleep medicine, nutrition, sports and exercise,
obesity, and behavior change and serves on the
editorial board of the American Journal of Lifestyle
Medicine (AJLM). He lives in Atlanta, Georgia, with
his wife and two cats and enjoys lifting weights, trail
running, and traveling.

JOHN KELLY, MD, MPH, LM Intensivist, FACLM

Dr. Kelly is trained in biochemistry, molecular biology, medicine, epidemiology, and
information technology. He completed studies at Loma Linda University in preventive
and lifestyle medicine and has done funded research in lifestyle medicine, was
founding President of ACLM, co-authored the inaugural and previous editions of

the Foundations of Lifestyle Medicine Board Review Manual and Course, and was

founding Chair for the Expert Lifestyle Medicine Panel. He received the American
Medical Association excellence in medicine award in 2004 for his work in establishing ACLM. He practices
lifestyle medicine and teaches clinicians lifestyle medicine around the world. Dr. Kelly established and
conducts lifestyle medicine training programs and serves as adjunct faculty at two medical schools.

ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS

This fourth edition of the Foundations of Lifestyle Medicine Board Review Manual for both the American and
the International Board of Lifestyle Medicine Certification Exams is the product of a collective, determined
effort involving many leaders and pioneers in lifestyle medicine. It draws upon much that has been done
before, building particularly upon the Lifestyle Medicine Core Competencies (LMCC) and related materials.
The authors want to especially thank those who contributed to that work, including Liana Lianov, MD, MPH,
DipABLM, FACPM, FACLM, and Mark Johnson, MD, MPH, who authored the 2010 JAMA article that first

put the LMCC in medical literature. Special thanks, too, to those who updated and authored the Lifestyle
Medicine Core Competencies: 2022 Update in AJLM.

The lead authors would like to extend their sincere appreciation to ACLM staff, Alexandra Kees, MPH, Senior
Education Project Manager, and Paulina Shetty, MS, RDN, DipACLM, Senior Director of Education for their
dedication to bringing this 4th edition manual and corresponding course to fruition. The authors additionally
want to thank the esteemed members of the expert Editorial Panel, contributing authors, reviewers, editors,
graphic designers, and ACLM staff who made important contributions that helped fill gaps and shape the
various editions of this product.

Expert Editorial Panel: Jonathan Bonnet, Marc Braman, Brenda Davis, Hans Diehl, David Drozek, Michael
Greger, and Scott Stoll.

ACLM Staff: Susan Benigas, Paulina Shetty, Alexandra Kees, Katie Edmiston, Andrea Westmoreland, Heather
Klein, Grace Gama, Micaela Karlsen, Kara Staffier, Kathy Pollard, and Leslie Casey.

Editors and Graphic Design: Abe Ogden, Medical Editor, and Rikki Campbell Ogden, Graphic Designer.

Thank you, thank you to each one! While the lead authors worked long and hard to make this course all it
could be, they simply could never have done it without the contributions and support of so many others. This
heartfelt gratitude is extended, as well, to the Ardmore Institute of Health, which provided seed funding that
enabled the first edition of this manual to be brought to fruition.

It is the authors’ intent for this course to not only enable clinicians to quickly master the core competencies
and pass their certification exam, but also to serve as a reference in the practice of lifestyle medicine and for
teaching lifestyle medicine to students, residents, and fellows. The authors intend to build upon this edition in
future editions that will continue to serve this two-fold purpose.

With the ardent hope and belief that lifestyle medicine must become the foundation of a transformed and

sustainable system of healthcare delivery, thank you for your commitment to educating and equipping
yourself to become champions for change in ushering in the future of health care.
